To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of Zn(HMTBa), Cu(HMTBa), and Mn(HMTB)2 in a diet containing corn and SBM improves the absorption and retention rates of Zn, Cu and Mn compared to inorganic Zn, Cu, or Mn, and that the use of FeGly in a corn-SBMDiet improves the retention of Fe compared to Fe sulfate.

Zn(HMTBA)2 has greater Zn digestibility and absorption than ZnSO4, Cu(HMTBA)3 has greater Cu digestibility and absorption, and Mn(HMTBA)4 has greater Mn digestibility and absorption in a corn-soybean diet.
Zn, Cu, Fe, and Mn from organic sources have greater absorption and retention rates than inorganic sources of these elements, especially in a corn-SB diet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the bioavailability of Zn, Cu and Mn in the form of organic microminerals.
the bioavailability of organic and inorganic microminerals in pigs fed either corn grits- or corn-SBM-based diets.
improving the efficiency of microminerals utilization by swine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the organic sources of Zn and Cu improved digestibility and retention of the minerals compared with their inorganics in the corn-SBM-based diets.
the organic forms of Zn, Cu and Mn are more digestible than the inorganic forms, and that the organic forms are more bio-available.
the organic forms of Zn, Cu and Mn have greater digestibility than the inorganic sources when included in a corn-soy diet, but that this is not the case when included in a grits based diet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
organic minerals are more digestible in corn-soybean-based diets, and that this effect is most pronounced for zinc.
the addition of OMM to the basal diet containing corn-SBM improved the digestibility of Zn, Cu and Mn, and P, and the retention rate for Zn, Cu, Fe, and P.
supplementation of OMM in a corn-SBMD improved the digestibility of Zn, Cu and Mn compared with supplementation of IMM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organic sources of microminerals have better digestibility and retention than inorganic sources of micromineral supplementation.
organic microminer-als are more digestible and retained than their inorganic counterparts.
organic forms of Zn, Cu and Mn are superior to their inorganic counterparts, but the organic forms of Fe are inferior to their inorganic counterpart.
